one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban shares his acceptance speech upon being named the Manila Overseas Press Club (MOPC) 'Journalist of the Year -- Law,' awarded on Oct 25 at the Fairmont Hotel, Makati -- the first such MOPC award in 78 years. The citation called him 'the No. 1 columnist of the Inquirer' with '12 [should be 14] books on law, faith, and the Supreme Court' for 'prolific work and prodigious excellence in writing about law and justice with depth, clarity, and command of language, thereby strengthening the people's faith in the third and often misunderstood branch of government, the judiciary.' Trophy details: bells ordered in Italy ('home to the world's oldest and best bell-manufacturing technology'), 15 inches tall, three kilos, symbolizing freedom, excellence, achievement, glory, perfection of craft. He shares the recognition with three 'Mega Media Movers': MOPC chair Tony Lopez (whose text invitation he initially answered 'I am not worthy... At best, I am just an ACCIDENTAL WRITER; in short, tsamba lang yon' -- and to whom he gave the title-quip 'Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious' to capture how lawyers 'tend to be highfalutin, muddled, and long-worded' while MOPC journalists 'write clearly and simply'); retired Inquirer chair Marixi R. Prieto, whom he first met in the late 1980s when she sold newsprint to the cash-strapped Inquirer and lent it P10 million convertible to common stock, becoming its 'ACCIDENTAL OWNER' when two deadlocked blocs assigned their holdings to her -- and who, on his 2006 retirement, invited him to write a column thrice a week, prompting Salonga's objection ('I do not know of any CJ who became a columnist. Chief justices do not write history; they make it.') and Marixi's retort ('I do not know of any chief justice who had been offered to write a regular column'), which inaugurated the 17-year, once-a-week streak through COVID (Dec 2022), Leni's death (April 9 -- whose eulogy became the most-visited Inquirer.net column as of August 2023), and international travel (e.g., Kuala Lumpur ALA speech), with first compilation volume (2011) ranked 3rd in Amazon's courts category behind Jeffrey Toobin and Antonin Scalia and royalties donated to the Inquirer Newsboy Foundation; and GMA Network chair and CEO Henry Gozon, whom he first knew as opposing counsel in aviation law (Gozon for PAL, author for KLM and Continental) some 50 years ago -- repeatedly invited to join the SC during the author's incumbency but respectfully declining, then visiting on Dec 6, 2006 with GMA president Jimmy Duavit to invite the author to GMA's board, and building GMA into the highest-rated Nielsen network with P7.5B record 2021 net profit under the 'Sa totoo lang tayo' motto. He closes feeling 'like receiving an honorary Ph.D. from the MOPC University of Journalism.'
